title: Stacks Browser per-item metadata (data/meta.json)
description: Per-item metadata merged by ui/js/corpus.js as it.meta. Definitions, anchors and classifier procedure: docs/meta/schema.md. Field paths must also pass the taxonomy check (levels 1-3 from x-taxonomy), which JSON Schema cannot express.

taxonomy.description: A copy of x-taxonomy, so the UI needs only meta.json.

field.description: Primary subject: 2-4 levels, levels 1-3 from the taxonomy, level 4 a specific free term.

formal.description: Proofs and derivations: 0 none, 1 some, 2 central.

empirical.description: Evidence from the world: 0 none, 1 cited or small-scale, 2 original data or experiments central.

code.description: Program code or pseudocode: 0 none, 1 snippets, 2 central.

by.description: Who classified it: 'calibration' or a model id.

note.description: Rationale for edge cases (calibration and audits; the UI ignores it).

empirical.label: Empirical study
empirical.def: New observations, experiments, measurements or data analysis are the main contribution.

method.label: Method
method.def: Proposes a technique, architecture, algorithm or system and shows it works.

theory.label: Theory
theory.def: Formal analysis is the contribution: definitions, derivations, theorems.

benchmark.label: Benchmark
benchmark.def: Introduces a benchmark, dataset or evaluation suite.

survey.label: Survey
survey.def: Maps a literature or landscape: review, taxonomy, synthesis, overview.

position.label: Position paper
position.def: A paper-form argument, agenda or proposal for what should be believed or done.

policy.label: Policy
policy.def: Lays down governance rules: lab frameworks, standards, draft treaties or laws, official policies.

report.label: Technical report
report.def: An organisation's account of its system or assessment: model reports and cards, eval or risk reports, incident reports.

essay.label: Essay
essay.def: Informal argument, reflection or exploration (blog posts, dialogues, transcripts).

explainer.label: Explainer
explainer.def: Teaches existing ideas or a practice in one sitting: tutorial, guide, primer.

textbook.label: Textbook
textbook.def: Book-length systematic teaching of established material; lecture notes and course texts.

monograph.label: Monograph
monograph.def: Book-length original work: treatise, research monograph, book-length argument.

handbook.label: Handbook
handbook.def: Practical manual for doing something: how-to, field manual, trade handbook.

reference.label: Reference
reference.def: Material to look things up in: wiki reference pages, glossaries, code books, tables, catalogues, indexes, bibliographies.

rules.label: Game rules
rules.def: Rules of a game: rulebooks, system reference documents.

periodical.label: Periodical
periodical.def: A journal, magazine, almanac or proceedings issue or volume.

collection.label: Collection
collection.def: Several independent works bound together: collected works, anthologies, miscellaneous papers.

puzzles.label: Puzzles & problems
puzzles.def: Problems, puzzles or exercises are the substance: puzzle books, problem sets, chess problems.

news.label: Announcement
news.def: Announces a launch, release, organisation, result or event.

x-stances.argues: Advocates a thesis; the gist states it.
x-stances.critiques: Argues against a specific claim, method, tool or work.
x-stances.proposes: Puts forward a new method, design, framework, institution or theory.
x-stances.reports: Presents findings, results, data or events with modest interpretation.
x-stances.surveys: Maps a body of work without a strong thesis.
x-stances.specifies: Lays down rules, protocols or procedures to follow.
x-stances.narrates: Tells a story: fiction, memoir, narrative history.
x-stances.records: Compiles reference material to be looked up: codes, tables, catalogues, periodical runs, quick references.

x-audiences.general: Any curious reader; no background assumed.
x-audiences.enthusiast: Informed amateurs and community insiders: LessWrong/EA readers, hobbyist players, puzzle fans.
x-audiences.student: Learners working through a subject: course texts, textbooks, primers.
x-audiences.practitioner: People applying the material: engineers, forecasters, analysts, officers, clerks, game masters.
x-audiences.researcher: Specialists in the field or an adjacent one.
x-audiences.policymaker: Decision-makers and policy staff in governments, labs and funders.

classic.def: Landmark: founded or defined a field or subfield and is still the reference everyone cites as the origin. Any age; rarely under 3 years.

historical.def: An ordinary period piece read today for history or curiosity (superseded manuals, code books, magazines). Never for landmarks.

established.def: Dated before 2022 and still read for its content.

frontier.def: Dated 2025-10 or later (the last 12 months before 2026-10) and working on an open question.

2.label: Informed
2.def: Some field vocabulary, explained or guessable; a curious reader of the community can follow.

3.label: Technical
3.def: A STEM-literate reader from the broad area can follow with effort; jargon used freely.

4.label: Specialist
4.def: Assumes working knowledge of the field (graduate level or practitioner).

5.label: Expert
5.def: Assumes the subfield's recent literature and formal machinery; written for the few working on it.

1.label: Arithmetic
1.def: Percentages, simple probabilities, tables, dice, back-of-envelope numbers.

2.label: School
2.def: Algebraic formulas, logs and exponents, odds and expected value, power laws and log-log plots, vectors as arrows.

3.label: Undergraduate
3.def: Calculus, linear algebra, probability distributions, ODEs, standard ML maths; derivations to follow.

4.label: Graduate
4.def: Measure-theoretic or advanced probability, functional and convex analysis, game-theoretic refinements, research-grade proofs.

5.label: Research
5.def: The mathematics is the content: specialist command of a mathematical field, proof-dense throughout.

x-reading.pace: Slowest that applies: P1 if tech<=2 and math<=1; P2 if tech 3 or math 2; P3 if tech 4 or math 3; P4 if tech 5 or math 4; P5 if math 5. formal 2 drops one step (floor P5). Fiction reads at P1.
x-reading.tables: Tables, code books and catalogues: 1 minute per page.
x-reading.scope: Main body only: exclude references, appendices, indexes, front matter and attached system cards.
x-reading.rounding: under 10: whole minutes; 10-120: nearest 5; 120-600: nearest 15; over 600: nearest 60.

AI.note: Artificial intelligence: safety, governance, language models, machine learning. AI forecasting lives under Forecasting.

Alignment.note: Technical AI safety: making AI goals, behaviour and internals safe, incl. agent foundations and safety engineering.

Language models.note: Capabilities research on LLMs: how they are built, trained, scaled, run and evaluated.

Machine learning.note: General machine learning outside LLM-specific work.

Forecasting.note: Making, aggregating, scoring and using forecasts and quantitative estimates, incl. forecasts about AI.

Quantitative estimation.note: Fermi models, probabilistic programming and cost-effectiveness modelling (QURI's Squiggle work lives here).

AI forecasting.note: Forecasts about AI: timelines, benchmark trends, takeoff, scenarios. Strategy given those forecasts goes to AI > Governance.

Epistemics.note: How individuals, institutions and processes reach good beliefs and judgments: rationality, evaluation, reasoning processes, discourse.

Rationality.note: LessWrong-style practical rationality. Academic psychology of bias goes to Psychology & self > Cognition.

Evaluation.note: Evaluating work, evaluators and evaluation systems (QURI Evaluation Engineering).

Reasoning processes.note: Designing robust judgment and oversight processes (QURI Robust Reasoning Processes).

Mathematics.note: Mathematics as subject matter (not as a tool used by another field).

Logic & foundations.note: Mathematical and symbolic logic. Traditional and inductive logic go to Philosophy > Logic & reasoning.

Game & decision theory.note: Mathematical game and decision theory. Philosophical decision theory goes to Philosophy; MIRI-style decision theory for AI agents to AI > Alignment > Agent foundations.

Calculation & numerical methods.note: Practical computation, calculating aids and their manuals.

Historical mathematics.note: Old mathematical texts read as sources: editions, translations, collected works.

Information theory.note: Shannon theory and its descendants: coding, compression, algorithmic information, information in learning and statistics.

Computing.note: Computer science and cryptography outside AI.

Cryptography.note: Ciphers and codebreaking of every era. Commercial (non-secret) telegraph codes go to Engineering > Telecommunications.

Systems & control.note: Cybernetics, control theory and systems theory, incl. their precursors.

Physics.note: Physics as subject matter, incl. historical physics texts.

Engineering.note: Applied technology and trades, incl. period manuals, codes and trade literature.

Social science.note: Economics, politics, global risk, effective altruism, communities, culture, education, military science.

Global catastrophic risk.note: Catastrophic and existential risk in general; AI-specific risk goes to AI.

Psychology & self.note: Minds, emotions, self-improvement, relationships and personal experience.

Logic & reasoning.note: Traditional, inductive and informal logic; reasoning manuals.

Decision theory.note: Philosophical decision theory. MIRI-style decision theory for AI agents goes to AI > Alignment > Agent foundations.

Games.note: Games as subject: tabletop RPGs, wargames, chess and board games, cards, game design.

Humanities.note: History, literature, linguistics, religion and the arts.

History.note: History as the main subject. History of a technical field goes under that field's own history node where one exists.
